item.label: High-angle pan left across low brick-on-edge wall with cavities and junctions
item.description: High-angle shot in outdoor sunlight looking down at a low, multi-course red clay brick wall structure resting on sandy soil. The bricks are laid on edge in parallel leaves with cross-bricks (headers/stretchers on edge) creating rectangular vertical hollow cavities visible along the open top course. Grey mortar dabs and joints bind the bricks, with fresh mortar droppings resting on the top edges and on the sandy ground at the base. At 0.00s–3.50s, the right corner return, main cavity wall section, and a metal mortar pan holding a red-handled trowel on the ground behind the wall are in view. From about 1.50s to 8.50s, the camera pans smoothly to the left across the T-junction and along a projecting partition/stub wall (whose top course has two parallel bricks on edge with an open gap between them), revealing another brick wall corner on the left side before settling slightly from about 8.50s to 9.130667s. No people or hands appear in frame.
item.context_result: The open top course clearly displays the internal hollow cavity geometry, staggered brick-on-edge bonding, corner arrangement, and T-junction intersection of the brickwork, alongside messy mortar droppings on the bricks and sandy floor.
item.camera_framing: High-angle close/medium overhead shot panning slowly from right to left.
item.uncertainty: Brick quality appears somewhat irregular with chipped corners, Frog marks on some faces, and rough mortar droppings; it cannot be verified from visuals alone whether this is a training/demonstration mock-up or part of an actual building foundation.

item.uncertainty: While the brick-on-edge cavity bond pattern is directly visible, the structure is built directly on bare sandy ground as a low demonstration course rather than a full-height habitable wall.
